title: Critical Encounters with "True Crime"
description: Investigates the history and theory of "true crime" as an evolving intermedial genre from early modern broadsides to 19th-century penny dreadfuls to contemporary podcasts, docuseries, and amateur digital investigations. Students will analyze "true crime" case studies through different lenses, such as economics and industry, aesthetics and pleasure, and ethics and representation.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis
description: A seminar for advanced students examining in-depth a particular problem or issue in the analysis of film and its consequences for history, theory, or aesthetics of film, television and digital media.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis Theme Park as Media Object
description: Introduces site-based research methods by exploring theme parks and attractions from a range of media studies perspectives. Students design projects that consider space and material alongside existing analytical frameworks, situating themed entertainment within the contemporary media landscape.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: The Selfie from Caravaggio to the Present
description: The digital “selfie" is ubiquitous. But what constitutes the lure of reproducing one’s image through technical media in the first place? This course examines histories and theories of self-imaging media, tracing how widespread concepts of selfhood have shifted over time alongside––and in relation to––the development of specific media technologies: from paintings to daguerreotypes, snapshots, cinema, video, and digital media. By analyzing broad tends and “case studies” of specific artists, filmmakers, and theorists; we will ultimately consider the historical context, and develop the conceptual skills, needed to survey and scrutinize ethical problems and potentials posed by selfies in the present.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Women in Film
description: Survey of the major debates on questions of women and representation in contemporary film criticism. Topics to be covered include the representation of sexuality and the family in the Hollywood cinema; feminism and the avant-garde
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Wirelessness
description: In this seminar, students consider the history, theory, and cultural politics of wireless communication technologies. Beginning in the 19th Century, when wireless communication technologies inspired potent fantasies ranging from the imperial to the occult, and tracing an arc to contemporary debates over such issues as wireless data security, this seminar explores the role of wirelessness in shaping popular understandings of the public and the private, the natural and the fabricated, and the secular and the spiritual.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Cinema and World War II
description: Examines film production and exhibition in the United States leading up to and during World War II. Topics include Warner Bros. anti-Nazi films, Disneys wartime cartoons, films on Japanese-American relocation, newsreels, and foreign film propaganda in the U.S.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Youth Culture
description: This seminar examines the origins and development of the American media's many preoccupations with youth, including as on-screen protagonists and a key demographic off-screen. Issues explored include: the terms and meanings of "youth media" and "youth culture"; themes associated with youth; and the ways producers have sought to attract youth.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Basic Screenwriting
description: A study of the creativity and the technique of screenwriting for the conventional narrative film and for TV. Students will be required to complete writing exercises, a treatment, and master scenes of a full-lengthproject.
prerequisites_raw: Consent of instructor, writing sample, upper-division standing.

title: Writing Adaptations
description: Theory and practice of adapting screenplays from other genres novels, stories, plays, poems, video games, comics, articles, etc. Lectures and readings in the theory of adaptation. Screenplays written in short form and/or long form, narrative and/or post-modern.
prerequisites_raw: Upper-division standing; consent of instructor.

title: Autobiographical Screenwriting
description: An approach to the basics of screenwriting: structure, story, characters, with an emphasis on developing a writing project derived from personal experience. Students are required to complete writing exercises, a treatment, and master scenes of a full-length project.
prerequisites_raw: Upper-division standing; consent of instructor.

title: Advanced Screenwriting
description: A course intended for students who have successfully completed Film Studies188A and have a full-length screenplay in process which they want to complete.
prerequisites_raw: Film Studies 188A.

title: Writing Short Films
description: An introduction to screenwriting, emphasizing the fundamentals of short film and T.V.: setup, climax and resolution, "character-driven" story and plot, the role of conflict, principles of action, exposition, and premise. Students are required to write two short films.
prerequisites_raw: Consent of instructor; upper-division standing.

title: Musical Theatre
description: An introduction to the unique techniques and challenges of writing for musical theatre, focusing on the collaborative art of telling a story through music, lyrics, script (the “book”) and dance. A historical overview of musical theater from early operetta to contemporary Broadway and West End hits, will inform our exploration of both the “show” and the “business.” Students will learn foundational vocabulary, analyze how songs advance character and plot, and develop scenes and songs in weekly, hands-on exercises, culminating in a workshop presentation of original works-in-progress.
prerequisites_raw: Upper-division standing.

title: Writing for New Media
description: Students write scenarios for video games, iPod videos, short internet videos/films, flash fiction, flash poetry, blogs, et. al. Readings provide understanding of new media in their historical, theoretical, and political-social contexts.
prerequisites_raw: Consent of instructor.
